question.text: At Piacenza, Alexios I was calling for help against the "Seljuk" variety of these people, who were themselves a subset of their "Ghuzz" variety. A group of "Young" ones rebelled against Sultan Abdul Hamid II in 1908.
question.clue: The "16 States" popularized by nationalists from this ethnic group include the Ghaznavids.

swap.leadin: Identify these historical people, who all hold the honorary title of 'father of the nation'.
swap.text: This man won the Turkish war of independence, and was the Republic of Turkey's first president. He gives his name to the ideology of Kemalism.
swap.answerHtml: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk [Accept Mustafa Kemal or Mustafa Kemal Pasha]
swap.clue: This man commanded the Nineteenth Division at the Battle of Gallipoli and founded his country's Grand National Assembly at Ankara.
swap.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

question.text: Under Article 301 of this country's penal code, it is forbidden to label the post-World War I deaths of Armenians as a genocide. It was home to an empire centered at Constantinople and was first led by Mustafa Ataturk.
question.clue: Herodotus, author of the Histories, was native of this modern-day country, as he was born in Halicarnassus.

swap.text: Ottoman authorities exterminated these people during World War One, often by marching them into the Syrian desert. These Christian people were considered of suspect loyalty by the Ottomans.
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.text: Name these units of infantry composed of former Christians converted to Islam by the devsirme system.
question.clue: When these people were eliminated, the closely-associated sect of Bektashi Sufism was banned.

swap.leadin: It is known as the first modern genocide.
swap.text: Name this holocaust that took place in the Ottoman Empire, which targeted a namesake group of Middle Eastern Christians.
swap.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide [or Armenian Massacre or Armenian Holocaust or The Great Calamity or The Great Crime or Ermeni Soykinmi or Mec Egert]
swap.clue: Despite the eforts of ambassador Henry Morgenthau Sr., the United States declined to intervene in this event.

question.text: Forces from New Zealand fought alongside those of Australia as part of the "Anzacs" during this disastrous 1916 British campaign in modern-day Turkey in World War I.
question.clue: William Birdwood coordinated his attack on Hill 60 with another assault on Scimitar Hill during this campaign, though both offensives failed.

swap.text: This sultan and rumored lover of Radu the Handsome presided over the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453. His armies thereby ended the Byzantine empire.
swap.answerHtml: Mehmet II [or Mehmet the Conqueror; or Mehmet el-Fatih; accept “Mehmed” for “Mehmet”]
swap.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

question.text: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.
question.answerHtml: Pasha [accept Three Pashas or İsmail Enver Pasha or Mehmed Talaat Pasha or Ahmed Cemal Pasha or Djemal Pasha]
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about developments in printing outside of Europe.
swap.text: Two edicts banning printing in the Ottoman empire were issued by Bayezid II and an emperor with this name. That emperor with this name conquered Egypt and was known as "the grim".
swap.clue: The first man to rule with this name was victorious at the Battle of Chaldiran over the Safavid ruler Isma'il I. A sultan of this name known as "The Blond" captured Cyprus but lost at Lepanto.

question.text: This son of Selim the Grim conquered Hungary after the Battle of Mohacs and defeated the Safavids. He was nicknamed "the Lawgiver" for his reforms.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman I [or Suleiman the Magnificent; or Sulayman al-Qanuni] [10] This sultan’s reign saw reforms known as the Tanzimat, such as the dissolution of the Janissaries in the Auspicious Incident and the adoption of more European-style dress and customs by the aristocracy. ANSWER: Mahmud II
question.clue: This ruler expelled the Knights Hospitalers from Rhodes after conquering Belgrade, although the same group would defeat him at Malta later on.

swap.leadin: John Julius Norwich's book Four Princes focuses on Charles V, Henry VIII, Francis I and this ruler.
swap.text: Name this ruler who patronized the prolific architect Sinan. The highly detailed Piri Reis world map was created during the reign of this ruler by one of his star admirals.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [accept Kanunî Sultan Süleyman; accept Suleiman the Lawgiver]
swap.clue: A principle known as the "circle of justice" guided the legal kanuns which he set up, and he supported the ascension of John Zapolya following one of his military victories.

question.text: The Janissaries were first organized in the 1360s under the rule of this first Ottoman sultan, who was killed at the battle of Kosovo.
question.clue: A Serbo-Magyar coalition that invaded his territory was crushed at the Battle of the Maritsa River.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Sevres demilitarized it until 3 years later, when the Treaty of Lausanne gave the rights of this body of water back to Turkey.
swap.text: Name this narrow strait which connects the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea, fought over several times in history.
swap.clue: In 1915 Winston Churchill arranged an attempt by Ian Hamilton to approach the contested site by land from its north.

question.leadin: This period saw the creation of the Arazi Kanunnamesi land code and efforts at promoting religious equality through the Imperial Reform Edict.
question.text: Name this period begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber.
question.clue: This period of reform in the Ottoman Empire begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. This period included the abolition of the millet system and the elimination of tax farming.

swap.text: The implementer of the Turkish surname law, Mustafa Kemal, took the surname Ataturk, while this "National Chief" who succeeded him took his surname from a town where he fought during the Greco-Turkish War.
swap.clue: This overall commander of Ottoman forces at Beersheba later received a surname drawn from the two 1921 battles where he forced invading Greeks to retreat. He was the successor of Ataturk as the second President of Turkey.

question.text: After being irked by the Treaty of Sevres, Ataturk pushed for the signing of this 1923 treaty, which offered more concessions to Turkey and established the nation's modern borders.
question.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

swap.leadin: Name these units of the Ottoman Army.
swap.text: The least prestigious unit of the Ottoman military consisted of these irregular, unprofessional soldiers. Their name translates to "damaged head", a reference to their lack of discipline.
swap.clue: This irregular Ottoman troops whose Turkish name means "disorderly heads" in reference to their tendency to loot. Gladstone's Midlothian campaign denounced these units' involvement in the "Bulgarian horrors."

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the decline and fall of the Ottoman Empire. Since Chris Ray apparently doesn't know what questions are, your reader will read these statements with a ridiculous and uncalled-for upwards inflection.
question.text: This period of reform introduced many European concepts of nationality to the empire, including the adoption of a national anthem and the creation of citizenship???
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.leadin: This man married the daughter of Prince Lazar, Olivera, after the Battle of Kosovo.
swap.text: Name this son of Murad I who was known as "the Thunderbolt." He defeated Sigismund at the Battle of Nicopolis.
swap.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.
